title: Network-Layer Primitives: Rate Limiting, Circuit Breaking, and Request Prioritisation
summary: Implements three C++20 header-only components that protect the Polymarket trading bot against Cloudflare HTTP 429 bursts, 5xx cascades, and order-sniping latency. All components are stack-only (zero heap allocation), deterministic via injectable clocks, and pass -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wshadow -Werror plus ASan/UBSan clean.

components.name: TokenBucket + RateLimiter
components.description: Fixed-point (milli-token) token bucket with multi-request-type support and exponential backoff. Prevents HTTP 429 bursts by gating order/cancel/query egress through per-type token buckets and doubling backoff on each rate-limited response (200→400→800ms, capped at backoff_max_ms).

TokenBucket: try_consume() — atomic CAS, O(1) hot path, returns bool
ms_until_available() — returns milliseconds until next token, 0 if available
refill() — lazy refill using integer milli-token accumulation
tokens_remaining() — current whole-token count for telemetry
reset() — restore bucket to full capacity
RateLimiter: can_send(RequestType) — checks backoff + token, consumes on success
on_sent(RequestType) — resets exponential backoff on success
on_rate_limited(RequestType, retry_ms) — doubles backoff, respects Retry-After
status() — RateStatus snapshot for ORDER type
types: RateLimitConfig { orders_per_sec, cancels_per_sec, queries_per_sec, burst_capacity, backoff_base_ms, backoff_max_ms, backoff_multiplier }

key_design_decisions: Milli-tokens (scale=1000) for sub-millisecond refill precision at any integer rate, using purely uint64_t arithmetic — no floating-point drift
std::atomic<uint64_t> for tokens and last_refill_ms with CAS-based refill claiming to prevent double-refill under contention
Backoff resets on on_sent() (success); each on_rate_limited() doubles the previous backoff starting from backoff_base_ms
ClockFn function-pointer injection enables deterministic unit tests without real sleeps

components.name: CircuitBreaker
components.description: State machine that trips OPEN after 3 consecutive failures (429/502/503/timeout), stays OPEN for 5000ms, then probes with 1 trial request (HALF_OPEN). Recovers to CLOSED after 2 successful probes, or returns to OPEN on any probe failure. When OPEN, trading_mode() returns CLOSE_ONLY, signalling WindowShield to force close-only mode.
api: on_success() — increments success counter in HALF_OPEN, may close circuit
on_failure() — increments failure counter, may open circuit
ms_until_retry() — remaining OPEN duration (0 when not OPEN)

state_machine.OPEN behaviour: allow_request() returns false; logs 'CB_OPEN: relying on TTL expiry'; trading_mode() == CLOSE_ONLY

key_design_decisions: Configurable thresholds with production defaults matching Polymarket 5m/15m window semantics
TradingMode enum provides a clean integration point with WindowShield for strategy-layer mode switching
Optional LogFn callback for observability (std::printf by default, null in tests)
All state is plain (non-atomic) — CircuitBreaker is called from a single trading thread

components.name: RequestPrioritizer
components.description: Four-band priority queue (CRITICAL > HIGH > NORMAL > LOW) backed by fixed-capacity ring buffers. Guarantees that order-cancellation and emergency-unwind requests are always dequeued before new entry orders or telemetry queries.
api: enqueue(Priority, id) — returns false if band is full (request is dropped)
dequeue() — returns Priority of the highest-priority pending request
last_id() — id of the most recently dequeued request
cancel(id) — O(n) removal across all bands, preserves FIFO within band
size(Priority) — count at a given priority level
empty() — true when all bands empty
key_design_decisions: FixedRingBuffer<64> per priority band = 256 uint32_t = 1 KiB total stack footprint
std::array-backed ring buffer with head/tail/count indices — no std::queue/deque/vector
cancel() uses linear scan + shift to preserve FIFO order within band
dequeue() checks bands in fixed priority order (CRITICAL→HIGH→NORMAL→LOW)
priority_order_ is a static constexpr std::array for zero runtime initialisation cost

build_verification.note: Full CMake build requires libsecp256k1 (already a hard dependency of the project). Standalone compile with g++ confirmed clean. CMake target configuration verified via a separate minimal CMake project.

integration_points.order_gateway: RateLimiter::can_send() gates each HTTP egress; on 429, on_rate_limited() is called. CircuitBreaker::allow_request() is checked before every send.
integration_points.window_shield: CircuitBreaker::trading_mode() returns CLOSE_ONLY when OPEN/HALF_OPEN. The strategy layer should combine this with WindowShield::current_state() to determine effective mode.
integration_points.execution_engine: RequestPrioritizer::dequeue() feeds the execution engine with priority-ordered requests, ensuring cancels and emergency unwinds are processed first.

known_limitations: CircuitBreaker is single-threaded (non-atomic state) — safe for the single-threaded hot path but not thread-safe.
RequestPrioritizer::cancel() is O(n) per band — acceptable for <64 pending requests, but degrades if the queue fills.
Backoff uses double for the multiplier — this is exact for multiplier=2.0 but could introduce sub-ULP drift for non-power-of-2 values (acceptable within backoff_max_ms cap).
